subject: Boot Hill
findings: The Hays municipal visitor bureau dates the cemetery's recorded burials to 1867-1874 and explicitly says early deaths included accidents and natural causes. Do not describe every person buried there as an outlaw or gunfighter.

Kansas Historical Society item 214513 is an 1885 excavation photograph, not a clear view of the cemetery during use. Actually viewed its 500-pixel archival image: disturbed open earth, workers, animals and wagons, with handwritten retrospective text. It does not resolve original grave-marker profiles well enough to brief a replica.

Modern Boot Hill displays and replacement markers cannot alone authenticate nineteenth-century grave forms or inscriptions. The 2021 Ogallala image from the Library of Congress is a candidate material reference, not period evidence; its image has not yet been visually reviewed.

Clement Wood's 1947 retrospective, republished by the Tombstone site, discusses wooden grave markers and later cemetery changes. It is not a contemporaneous 1880 image and must be identified as later testimony.
